verses.html: Then Job answered and said,
verses.text: Then Job answered and said,

verses.html: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?
verses.text: I know it is so of a truth: but how should man be just with God?

verses.html: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.
verses.text: If he will contend with him, he cannot answer him one of a thousand.

verses.html: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?
verses.text: He is wise in heart, and mighty in strength: who hath hardened himself against him, and hath prospered?

verses.html: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.
verses.text: Which removeth the mountains, and they know not: which overturneth them in his anger.

verses.html: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.
verses.text: Which shaketh the earth out of her place, and the pillars thereof tremble.

verses.html: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.
verses.text: Which commandeth the sun, and it riseth not; and sealeth up the stars.

verses.html: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.
verses.text: Which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea.

verses.html: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.
verses.text: Which maketh Arcturus, Orion, and Pleiades, and the chambers of the south.

verses.html: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.
verses.text: Which doeth great things past finding out; yea, and wonders without number.

verses.html: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.
verses.text: Lo, he goeth by me, and I see him not: he passeth on also, but I perceive him not.

verses.html: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?
verses.text: Behold, he taketh away, who can hinder him? who will say unto him, What doest thou?

verses.html: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.
verses.text: If God will not withdraw his anger, the proud helpers do stoop under him.

verses.html: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?
verses.text: How much less shall I answer him, and choose out my words to reason with him?

verses.html: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.
verses.text: Whom, though I were righteous, yet would I not answer, but I would make supplication to my judge.

verses.html: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.
verses.text: If I had called, and he had answered me; yet would I not believe that he had hearkened unto my voice.

verses.html: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.
verses.text: For he breaketh me with a tempest, and multiplieth my wounds without cause.

verses.html: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.
verses.text: He will not suffer me to take my breath, but filleth me with bitterness.

verses.html: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?
verses.text: If I speak of strength, lo, he is strong: and if of judgment, who shall set me a time to plead?

verses.html: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.
verses.text: If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me: if I say, I am perfect, it shall also prove me perverse.

verses.html: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.
verses.text: Though I were perfect, yet would I not know my soul: I would despise my life.

verses.html: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.
verses.text: This is one thing, therefore I said it, He destroyeth the perfect and the wicked.

verses.html: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.
verses.text: If the scourge slay suddenly, he will laugh at the trial of the innocent.

verses.html: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?
verses.text: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof; if not, where, and who is he?

verses.html: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.
verses.text: Now my days are swifter than a post: they flee away, they see no good.

verses.html: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.
verses.text: They are passed away as the swift ships: as the eagle that hasteth to the prey.

verses.html: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:
verses.text: If I say, I will forget my complaint, I will leave off my heaviness, and comfort myself:

verses.html: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.
verses.text: I am afraid of all my sorrows, I know that thou wilt not hold me innocent.

verses.html: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?
verses.text: If I be wicked, why then labour I in vain?

verses.html: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;
verses.text: If I wash myself with snow water, and make my hands never so clean;

verses.html: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.
verses.text: Yet shalt thou plunge me in the ditch, and mine own clothes shall abhor me.

verses.html: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.
verses.text: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment.

verses.html: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.
verses.text: Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both.

verses.html: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:
verses.text: Let him take his rod away from me, and let not his fear terrify me:

verses.html: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.
verses.text: Then would I speak, and not fear him; but it is not so with me.
